PAINTING & BODYWORK · Restoration

Body Restoration in Riyadh

Body restoration for valued and classic vehicles in Riyadh — corrosion, old repairs and tired bodywork brought back methodically, with the scope agreed stage by stage.

  1. Home
  2. Painting & Bodywork
  3. Body Restoration

Restoration is slow truth-telling: beneath old paint there is always more story — previous repairs, filler, corrosion, panels that were never quite right. QSC approaches body restoration in agreed stages, documenting what each layer reveals and deciding the next step with the owner rather than for them. Whether the car is a cherished classic or simply a vehicle worth keeping right, the goal is a body that is honest underneath, not just shiny on top.

Restoration planning starts from purpose, because purpose defines standard: a preservation car wants original material saved wherever honesty allows; a driver-grade restoration wants durability and correctness over concours perfection; a show car accepts cost and time that neither of the others would. QSC opens every restoration with that conversation, then structures the project into stages whose findings gate the next step. The owner approves each stage knowing what the last one revealed — the opposite of the open-chequebook restorations that sour owners on the whole exercise.

Gulf cars bring a particular restoration profile: less structural rust than European or coastal vehicles, but deep UV damage to paint and trim, heat-cracked seals and plastics, and often a history of quick cosmetic repairs layered over decades. Stripping those layers honestly — documenting each one — regularly reveals a better car than feared or a worse one than hoped, and either truth is worth having early. The photographic record built through the project becomes part of the car's provenance, with real value at sale time for collectible vehicles.

When to book this service

  • Corrosion appearing on sills, arches, or around glass and seams
  • An older or classic vehicle you want brought back properly
  • Previous repairs — filler, overspray, mismatched panels — surfacing with age
  • A car worth preserving whose body needs more than a repaint

How QSC handles it

Staged assessment, with findings documented photographically as layers come off

Corrosion treatment and metalwork done properly, not cosmetically

Panel repair, replacement or fabrication-level correction as agreed per stage

Refinishing to a standard agreed for the car's purpose — driver, show or preservation

Why QSC for this service

  • Purpose-first planning: preservation, driver or show standard set before work begins
  • Staged scope with approval gates — findings control the budget, not momentum
  • Gulf-specific expertise: UV, heat and layered old repairs more than structural rot
  • A photographic provenance record with genuine resale value

Cost and time — honestly

Pricing at QSC follows the assessment, never precedes it: after evaluation you receive the proposed scope and its cost for approval, and only what you approve is carried out. Durations are estimated realistically per job — we publish no blanket promises we could not keep for every case.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Can you give a fixed price for a restoration?

Honestly, no responsible shop can before the car is opened up. What QSC gives instead is a staged scope: each stage has an agreed extent and cost, and what stage one reveals shapes stage two — with your approval in between.

How long does restoration take?

It depends entirely on what is found and the standard you want. Timeframes are discussed per stage rather than promised for the whole project up front.

Is restoration only for classic cars?

No — a ten-year-old luxury car with corrosion or bad previous repairs is a restoration candidate too. The method is the same; only the scale differs.

Can I do the restoration in phases over time?

Yes — staged projects suit many owners and budgets, with natural pause points designed in. The sequencing matters (structure and corrosion before cosmetics, always), and we plan storage or drivable intervals between phases so the car is never stranded mid-project.
